merged_body: Full-review audit epics (angr-9ke6b, angr-sqfj8, angr-12jjk and their successors) file their child beads against a snapshot tree, and both their PREMISES and their CODE CITATIONS rot fast once sibling beads start landing. Round-2 epics angr-sqfj8 and angr-12jjk OVERLAP: five consecutive ralph iterations (120-124) claimed a bead whose premise was already fixed or duplicated (angr-sqfj8 .55, .54, .51, .48); angr-sqfj8.48 (DRY the LengthLimiter/LoopBound eviction arms) was landed verbatim by angr-12jjk.20 the same week. The angr-9ke6b children were filed 2026-07-31 against a pre-e2da4c1fa tree and their code citations measurably rotted: at iter149, angr-9ke6b.201 cited 'cfg_fast.py:1454-1457: idx = search(...) then self._seg_list[idx]' as SegmentList::search's live consumer, but that site had become _nodecode_bytes_ratio using iter_backward_from, leaving search() with zero in-tree callers outside segmentlist_tests.rs (filed as angr-9ke6b.232). RULE: before editing for any audit-epic child bead, open the cited site and re-verify the premise; if already fixed, 'git log -S<symbol> -- <file>' finds the fixing commit, then close with a bd note naming the canonical bead rather than making a code change. Grep for the cited symbol before writing a doc/comment that repeats the bead's caller claim, or you bake a stale citation into the source -- exactly the class tools/check_line_citations.py exists to stop. Audit epics are containers: descend to leaves, never claim the epic row.
